title: Request Recon Lens: Compact multi-span drilldown + correlation inspector
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Goal: design a compact, cognition-friendly request drilldown ("Request Recon Lens") that surfaces span relationships, correlation IDs across services, per-request cost sparkline, and active rollout metadata without forcing users into a full-page trace viewer. The lens should be embeddable in dashboards and A/B rollout pages so engineers and PMs can quickly validate regressions, cost spikes, and rollout impacts next to metrics.

Scope: sketch and prototype the compact lens and the expanded inspector state, define the interaction model for span stacking and context pinning, propose accessibility-friendly color/state mapping for failures/warnings, and provide handoff artifacts for ENG to implement the minimal runtime payload needed (span slice, kv-context, rollout-labels, cost-estimate).
acceptance_criteria: Compact lens renders inline inside a dashboard card with up to 10 visible spans and a compact time ruler
Users can expand any span to inline span details (start/duration, tags, KV snippets) without navigating away
Correlation ID search highlights matching spans across the mini-view and allows jump-to-full-trace
Rollout annotations appear as badges on spans and are filterable by release variant
Per-request cost sparkline (last 5 samples) is present and links to cost breakdown in Console
Prototype validated in a 5-person usability pass with at least 80% success on locating root cause in a seeded failure scenario
comments: 2026-03-03 - Asha Patel: Initial discovery complete. Spoke with Observability team about minimal span payload; they recommended adding a 'kv_preview' field limited to 256 chars to avoid large payloads.
2026-03-05 - Ethan Brooks: ENG can provide slice endpoints; flagged performance risk when embedding >20 lenses on a single dashboard. Suggested server-side aggregation and a 'sparse' mode.
2026-03-06 - Maya Sanchez: Request from Growth to include rollout variant tag for any request coming from canary. Marked as high-visibility for next week's trial.
2026-03-08 - Asha Patel: Uploaded Figma flows. Prototype includes two compact states: collapsed (sparkline + 3-span summary) and expanded inline (stacked spans with correlation lane).

2026-03-09 - Nora Kim: Accessibility review: color-only failure indicators are insufficient. Recommend adding iconography plus ARIA labels. Also requested 3:1 contrast for sparkline against background when focused.
2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connor: Design review notes: prefer vertical stacking with sticky time ruler on expand; ask ENG for hook to prefetch full-trace on hover to speed jump-to-full-trace.
2026-03-11 - Ethan Brooks: ENG review: agreed to add prefetch hook and a 'sparse' belt endpoint. Added ticket ENG-20821 to implement sampling and cost estimate endpoint.
2026-03-12 - Maya Sanchez: PM review: prioritize rollout badge filter and cost sparkline for initial canary trial. Approved prototype for testing with internal SRE team.
decisions: Use an inline compact card that expands to an inline inspector rather than full-page by default
Show up to 10 spans in the compact view; use vertical stacking and compressive visual encoding for short spans
Add rollout badges pulled from rollout metadata (release.variant) and make them filterable at the card level
Cost sparkline uses latest 5 request samples; clicking opens cost breakdown panel in Console
Accessibility: add icons + ARIA labels for span states and ensure keyboard expand/collapse
open_questions: What is the acceptable maximum payload size for embedded lenses to keep dashboard render times < 300ms?
Should we show KV preview by default or behind a hover/expand to reduce visual clutter and payload size?
How should we surface multi-correlation IDs when a request has >1 correlation header?
